# Patient state and the two modes

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

This module holds the patient's shared state: the 21 state variables (heart rate, pressures, saturation, ventilation,
temperature, potassium, QTc and others) with their defaults and limits, the instructor's target ramps, and the pin,
release and control flags. In MANUAL mode the instructor sets these targets directly; in MODELED mode the physiology
models own the values and a pin holds a variable. An embedding developer also reads it for the opt-in `truth` event,
a pruned copy of the pipeline state for developer tools.
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- Each state variable has a default adult value and a minimum and maximum, and in MANUAL mode is either an instructor
  target or derived by a coupling rule (brief §4.9; research 03 §2, §3.2; `l1/state.ts`).
- A target change starts a new ramp from the current value, so a retarget in mid-ramp never jumps; the ramp runs from
  its start plus an optional delay over its duration, and a zero-duration step takes effect at its start
  (brief §4.9; `l1/ramp.ts`, `l1/state.ts`).
- The ramp shape is linear, exponential with τ = duration/3 normalised to reach exactly 1, or logistic with its
  10–90 % rise in the middle of the ramp (brief §4.9; `l1/ramp.ts`).
- Control flags rank override (a coupling rule holding the value away from its target) above pinned above ramping
  (brief §4.9 "Control flags"; `l1/state.ts`).
- Releasing a pin keeps the value; MODELED mode then blends it back to the model (`l1/state.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->
